- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.6) and recent history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.4) or shows negative drift, especially after recent spikes.
- Avoid sharp upward forecasts following strong sentiment spikes; prices often correct or retrace within 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model tends to overreact; cap forecast peaks at 1–2% above recent 7-day high.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Lagged bias: if forecast is >10% above true outcome 3 days prior, adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for next forecast.
- Overshoot after spikes: if true outcome drops >5% from forecast peak, reduce next forecast by 1–3% to avoid overcorrection.
- Sentiment-driven momentum: if sentiment >0.7 and price is rising, forecast should be conservative; if sentiment <0.3 and price is falling, forecast should be aggressive.
